headline: 2 crude bombs blast in AL procession in Gulshan, 2 held
summary: Police arrested two people and recovered five additional crude bombs after activists of the banned Awami League attempted to hold a procession in Dhaka.
details: Two crude bombs were detonated during a procession by activists of the banned Awami League in Dhaka’s Gulshan area yesterday.
Around 150-200 people attempted to bring out the procession on Road 3 of Gulshan 1 around 11:45 am, according to Gulshan Police Station OC Daud Hossain.
When police tried to disperse the crowd, activists blasted two crude bombs, leading police to fire two rounds of rubber bullets to disperse the group.
Police arrested two individuals from the spot and recovered five more crude bombs left behind by the activists.
The Awami League's Dhaka city north unit confirmed via a Facebook post that they had organized the procession.

headline: Gold prices rise by ৳1,050 per bhori after one day
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) announced the new rates effective from Saturday morning, citing global market trends and a weak US dollar.
details: Gold prices in Bangladesh have increased by ৳1,050 per bhori within a single day. This follows a sharp decrease of ৳2,158 per bhori on Friday, making the new rates effective as of 10 AM Saturday.
According to the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS), the price adjustment was driven by an increase in the price of fine gold in local markets and a rise in gold prices on the global market.

The price of one bhori of high-quality 22-carat gold is now ৳232,930, while 21-carat gold is priced at ৳222,491. 18-carat gold stands at ৳191,056 and traditional gold is ৳156,640 per bhori, including VAT.
For comparison, the previous prices were ৳231,880 for 22-carat, ৳221,441 for 21-carat, ৳189,123 for 18-carat, and ৳156,306 for traditional gold.
While gold prices rose, silver prices decreased by ৳116 per bhori, bringing the price of 22-carat silver to ৳5,016 per bhori.
The domestic market has seen significant volatility. Gold reached its historic high of ৳286,000 per bhori on January 29 this year, after a sudden jump of ৳16,213 in one morning.

Analysts suggest that current price hikes are primarily due to a weak US dollar rather than geopolitical tensions in the Persian Gulf. Despite rising interest rates in the US, the dollar's value has not increased.
Global gold prices have fluctuated recently, with a decrease of $17 per ounce last Friday, but an overall increase of $2.59 per ounce over the last 30 days.
